title: RabbitMQ, Amazon SQS and SNS: when a queue beats a log

videos.script: Six orders come in from the website. Each one has to be packed, once, by one person in the warehouse. {{orders}} That is not an event for many readers. It is work, and when it is done, nobody needs the message again. {{work}} A queue is built for that. Each message goes to one worker. When the worker says done, the message is deleted. {{queue}} If the worker dies first, the message goes to somebody else. Nothing is lost, and something may be done twice. {{redelivery}} What a queue cannot do is go back. A reader that arrives tomorrow finds nothing from today. {{replay}} In this lesson you run RabbitMQ, route messages through exchanges, and catch the ones nobody could handle. {{rabbit}} Then the same ideas as a service, with SQS and SNS, on an emulator. And a table for choosing between a queue and a log. {{choose}}
